newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs easier on official comments.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs easier on official comments.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures remained bruised in late Wednesday trade after a flurry of apparently contradictory comments by Japanese government officials left the market without any clear signals, dealers said.

December JGBs fell to a low of 124.68 earlier in the day on comments by senior government officials who said recent rises in yen bond prices were not in line with the performance of the economy, in which production had begun to show some strength.
Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said in his weekly news conference the economic recovery was becoming solid but indicated it was not yet self-sustaining.
"The comments provided some volatility but they all offered nothing affirmative," said a trader with an Asian institution. "Matsushita's comments were neutral to bearish for the market."
Late in the afternoon, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference Japan's long-term rates reflected economic fundamentals.
Dealers said Mitsuzuka's statement seemed to suggest there was no need for a Japanese interest rate hike at present, giving a brief boost to the market, but December JGBs failed to get above 125.00.
They settled at 124.73 against their previous 125.39. The lead June Euroyen contract stood at its day low of 99.19 at 1120 GMT against its IMM close at 99.22.

A broker with a European futures house said players were turning wary on the Japanese bond market ahead of the BOJ's quarterly tankan survey and the Finance Ministry's two- and 10-year bond auctions next week.

"A lot of people are looking to set up shorts. On the options market, there's a lot of put-buying and call-selling, which would have been unthinkable a few weeks ago," he said. "(December JGBs) are a definite sell above 126.00."
Eurodollar futures ended little moved after an overnight rally on U.S. treasury markets where a drop in October housing starts confirmed recent signs of a slowing economy.

Dealers said the market would be keeping an eye on Wednesday's U.S. five-year note auction and international trade data for September. March Eurodollars ended unchanged at 94.50 on light volume of 4,040 lots.
